sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
Heard Mr. Alauddin, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.

This bail application has been filed by the applicant Ajijullah, seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 107 of 2023, under Sections 323, 363, 366, 376, 504 IPC and Sections 5/6 POCSO Act, P.S. Itwa, District Siddharth Nagar, during pendency of the trial.
Perused the record.
At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that notice of present application for bail has been served upon first informant opposite party 4.
However, in spite of service of notice, no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant opposite party 4 to oppose this application for bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred in between 7.5.2023 to 21.5.2023, a delayed F.I.R. dated 14.6.2023 was lodged by first informant Rukhsana, (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 107 of 2023, under Sections 323, 363, 366, 376 IPC and Sections 5/6 POCSO Act, P.S. Itwa, District Siddharth Nagar,

In the aforesaid F.I.R.,
applicant Ajijullah has been nominated as solitary named accused.

The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that named accused came to the house of the first informant on 7.5.2023 at around 8 a.m. and thereafter enticed away the minor daughter of the first informant i.e. prosecutrix namely X aged about 16 years.

The F.I.R. further records that the named accused thereafter deliberately dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix and ultimately after beating her, dropped the prosecutrix in front of village on 21.5.2023.
Subsequent to above F.I.R., Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr. P. C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr. P. C., which is on record at page 32 of the paper book.

The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has supported the F.I.R. to the effect that there was love affair in between the applicant and the prosecutrix but by extending false promise of marriage, he deliberately dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix by forcibly maintaining physical relation with her on 6.5.2023 and thereafter, the parents of the applicant are said to have refused to solemnize marriage of the applicant with the prosecutrix.
Subsequent
to above, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her has rejoined her previous statement recorded under Section 161 Cr. P. C.
The Doctor, who examined the prosecutrix did not find any injury on her body so as to denote commission of sexual assault.

With regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor opined as follows:-
"Hymen Old torned"
As per the medical opinion, the prosecutrix is said to be aged about 17 years.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr. P. C., which is on record at page 34 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has supported her earlier statements but with the improvements that the applicant has also refused to solemnize marriage with the prosecutrix.

During course of investigation, Investigating Officer recovered the certificate issued by the Principal of Km. Vidya Mandir High School Goandevi Mandir Road, Dhaniv Baug, Nallasopara (E) District Palghar, wherein the date of birth of the prosecutrix is recorded as 12.4.2007.
The occurrence giving rise to the present application is said to have occurred on 7.5.2022.
As such, the prosecutrix was aged 15 years and 25 days on the date of occurrence.
Investigating Officer also examined the first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr. P. C., who have supported the F.I.R.

On the basis of above and other material collected by him during course of investigation,
he came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant is established in the crime in question.
Accordingly, Investigating Officer submitted the charge sheet.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant contends that though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
The prosecutrix is aged about 17 years as per the medical opinion.
Furthermore, she is a willing and consenting party.
The police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr. P. C. has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, upto this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
Applicant is in jail since 19.6.2023.
As such, he has undergone 2 months of incarceration approximately.
He, therefore, contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since the applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 17 years whose modesty has been repeatedly dislodged on the false promise of marriage.
As per the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr. P. C., the applicant is alleged to have resiled from the promise so extended.
It is thus contended that no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.

Reference has also been made to the following judgements of the Supreme Court:-
(1) Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and another, 2019 SCC OnLine SC 1073 (2) Maheshwar Tigga Vs. State of Jharkhand, (2020) 10 SCC 108 (3)
Sonu alias Subhash Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 181 (4) The judgement of the Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No(s). 442/2022

sentences.text:
( Mandar Deepak Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra and another) (5) Naim Ahamed Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89 Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for state, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, complicity of the accused, accusation made, nature and gravity of offence and coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix is admittedly below 18 years of age, the modesty of the prosecutrix has been repeatedly dislodged by the applicant on the false promise of marriage, as per the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr. P. C., the applicant is said to have resiled from the promise so made,
the ocular version of the occurrence is clearly corroborated by the medical evidence particularly the recital occurring at page 49 of the paper book, therefore, irrespective of submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant but without making any comments on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result, present application for bail fails and is liable to be rejected.
It is, accordingly, rejected.
